allies.rationale_text: Probabilistic-thinking gives confidence-calibration the language of ranges and uncertainty so confidence can be expressed as earned odds rather than vibes.
allies.source_quote: Thinking in bets means acknowledging that decisions are inherently probabilistic and based on imperfect beliefs.
allies.affinity_rationale: Core mechanism — 'Thinking in bets means acknowledging that decisions are inherently probabilistic and based on imperfect beliefs' — probabilistic thinking IS the cognitive mode that makes calibration meaningful rather than just hedging.
allies.activation_condition: When confidence estimates need to be treated as probabilistic beliefs rather than binary certainties, and communicating uncertainty invites genuine updating

allies.rationale_text: Base-rates anchor confidence-calibration to the outside view so conviction is disciplined by what tends to happen in the world.
allies.source_quote: Calibration anchors the inside view (personal perspective) to the outside view (what is generally true in the world).
allies.affinity_rationale: Calibration anchor — 'anchors the inside view to the outside view' and 'accuracy lives at the intersection of these two views' — base rates provide the external reality check that prevents calibration from drifting into subjective comfort.
allies.activation_condition: When personal confidence needs to be anchored to population-level frequencies so that the inside view is calibrated against what is generally true rather than what feels true from personal experience

allies.rationale_text: Decision-trees benefit from confidence-calibration because branch precision is only trustworthy when the branch probabilities have actually been earned.
allies.source_quote: Most useful when a decision tree, integration model, or capital-allocation spreadsheet is carrying more certainty than the evidence base has earned.
allies.affinity_rationale: Structural tool — 'Most useful when a decision tree, integration model, or capital allocation decision' — provides the framework for applying calibrated probabilities to branching outcomes, but operates as an application tool.
allies.activation_condition: When calibrated probability estimates need to be applied across branching decision paths to compare expected values of alternative courses of action

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias corrupts confidence-calibration by defending a favored belief instead of updating confidence against disconfirming evidence.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Direct opposition — 'Calibration directly opposes confirmation bias' — the drive to defend existing beliefs prevents the honest uncertainty assessment that calibration demands.
antagonists.activation_condition: When the drive to defend existing beliefs is causing confidence estimates to be inflated in the direction of the preferred conclusion rather than honestly assessed

antagonists.rationale_text: Anchoring can freeze confidence-calibration around an early estimate so later evidence fails to widen or narrow the range appropriately.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Miscalibration vector — 'Unwarranted Optimism / Planning Fallacy / Anchoring' — initial estimates create a reference point that prevents proper recalibration as new evidence arrives.
antagonists.activation_condition: When an initial confidence estimate is resisting adjustment despite accumulating evidence because the original anchor is exerting disproportionate pull on subsequent estimates

structured_tensions.tension_text: Confidence-calibration conflicts with bias-blind-spot when calibration exercises create false assurance that one's judgments are now bias-free.
structured_tensions.source_quote: confidence-calibration conflicts with bias-blind-spot (bias blind spot) when calibration exercises create false assurance that one's judgments are now bias-free.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Confidence-calibration conflicts with authority-bias when well-calibrated confidence in one domain is transferred uncritically to domains where the calibrator lacks expertise.
structured_tensions.source_quote: confidence-calibration conflicts with authority-bias (authority bias) when well-calibrated confidence in one domain is transferred uncritically to domains where the calibrator lacks expertise.
